rationale: Tier S: Scrapy is a full-featured, production-stable web crawling framework (v2.17.0, BSD-3-Clause). 175 Python source files across 87 directories with 292 test files covering engine, scheduler, downloader, scraper, selector, middleware (downloader/spider), item pipelines, feed exporters, extensions, link extractors, and commands. Architectural docs exist at docs/topics/architecture.rst and docs/topics/components.rst. The Twisted-async engine architecture supports concurrent requests, per-domain slots, retry, redirect, HTTP proxy, cookie handling, robots.txt compliance, offsite filtering, HTTP/2, and sitemap-driven crawl. Relevance to a scraping pipeline extracting structured laptop specs is very high: Scrapy provides the crawl orchestration (scheduler with priority queues, dupefilter, depth control), download (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, FTP, file/data URI handlers), and extraction infrastructure (CSS/XPath selectors via parsel, link extractors, item pipelines, feed export). Of the eight Veridian pipeline concerns: queue (direct match — Scrapy has a full scheduler with priority queues, disk/memory queues, and job persistence via queuelib); script-generation (partial — spiders are Python classes with parse callbacks, not LLM-generated scripts, but the spider abstraction is extensible); self-healing (indirect — retry middleware, redirect following, and fallback mechanisms exist but no adaptive selector healing); stealth (limited — user-agent rotation, proxy middleware, cookie handling exist but no fingerprint randomization, browser-emulation, or anti-bot evasion beyond basic HTTP-level controls). No JSON-LD/Schema.org extraction, no browser automation engine, no fuzzy matching/dedupe library, no full-text search index. RelevanceScore 9.5: essential foundation for any crawling pipeline, missing only the Veridian-specific extraction and automation layers.
limitations: No JSON-LD / Schema.org extraction capability in source tree (grep for json-ld, jsonld, schema.org, microdata, rdfa returned zero hits in .py files under scrapy/)

No browser automation engine — no Playwright, Selenium, Puppeteer, or Splash integration in source tree (grep returned only BrowserLikePolicyForHTTPS TLS context factory and view-in-browser utility, both unrelated to browser automation)
No stealth/anti-bot evasion beyond standard HTTP middleware (user-agent setting, proxy, cookie) — no fingerprint randomization, TLS fingerprinting, or undetected-browser patterns found
No LLM script generation — spiders are hand-authored Python classes, not generated by LLM prompts
No fuzzy matching or approximate string comparison beyond URL canonicalization — no fuzzywuzzy, levenshtein, ratcliff, soundex, or similar in source
No full-text search index — no Elasticsearch, Whoosh, Solr, or Lucene integration in source tree
No self-healing selectors — no adaptive XPath/CSS recalibration on DOM change
Does not natively extract laptop specs or any domain-specific structured data — spiders must be authored per target
Twisted-based async model may differ from asyncio-native pipelines but does support asyncio reactor
evidencePaths: scrapy/core/engine.py (data flow orchestrator with async support)
scrapy/core/scheduler.py (priority queue scheduler with disk/memory backends, dupefilter, job persistence)
scrapy/core/downloader/__init__.py (per-domain concurrency slots, delay, retry orchestration)
scrapy/core/scraper.py (response parsing pipeline with spider middleware)
scrapy/exporters.py (JSON, CSV, XML, pickle, marshal export)
scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/ (retry, redirect, proxy, user-agent, cookie, cache, robots, offsite)
docs/topics/architecture.rst (architecture overview with data flow diagram)
pyproject.toml (dependencies: Twisted, lxml, parsel, cssselect, queuelib, protego)
tests/ (292 test files covering all major subsystems)
